survey: A cowboy lasso seen from the front, as if lying flat or hanging. Left: a coil of about four turns of twisted yellow rope, held together at the top by a red tie wrapped twice around the bundle, with its two ends crossed in an X. Bottom of the coil: one rope end hooks over the front of the coil and hangs straight down, finished with a cream whipping cap. Lower right of the coil: the running strand comes out, crosses a short gap and enters a cream honda (eyelet). From the honda the rope forms a large oval noose on the right, and both ends of the noose meet at the honda. The overall layout of coil, honda and noose matches a real lasso. Every rope end finishes at the cap, the tie or the honda, so there are no loose ends and nothing floats.

errors.where: Left coil, especially its left and inner side
errors.what: The coil is not made of separate, even turns. The strands are thick and clearly separate on the right but thin out and merge into one crescent on the left, so the turns melt into each other instead of reading as distinct loops of one rope.

errors.where: Lower right of the coil, where the strand leaves for the honda
errors.what: The strand that runs to the honda has no clear starting point. It seems to come out from behind or inside the coil rather than continuing from the outermost turn, so the rope's path from the coil to the noose cannot be followed.

fix: Draw the coiled lasso as 4 to 5 even, distinct turns of rope of the same thickness all the way around, each turn clearly separate. Make the running strand to the honda a visible continuation of the outermost turn.
